Blocks.Text: LinkedIn is a powerful platform to share content with your social network. Ensure your content receives the professional audience it deserves using Share on LinkedIn.
Use Share on LinkedIn to:

Get your content in front of an audience of millions of professionals.
Drive traffic to your site and grow your member base.
Benefit from having your content shared across multiple professional networks worldwide.

New members Sharing on LinkedIn from your application for the first time will need to follow the Authenticating with OAuth 2.0 Guide. When requesting an authorization code in Step 2 of the OAuth 2.0 Guide, make sure to request the w_member_social scope!

Rows.Text: Required to create a LinkedIn post on behalf of the authenticated member.

Blocks.Text: After successful authentication, you will acquire an access token that can be used in the next step of the share process.

If your application does not have this permission, you can add it through the Developer Portal. Select your app from My Apps, navigate to the Products tab, and add the Share on LinkedIn product which will grant you w_member_social.

There are multiple ways to share content with your LinkedIn network. In this guide, we will show you how to create shares using text, URLs, and images. For all shares created on LinkedIn, the request will always be a POST request to the User Generated Content (UGC) API.
POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/ugcPosts
Note
All requests require the following header: X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0

Rows.Text: The author of a share contains Person URN of the Member creating the share. See Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect to see how to retrieve the Person URN.
Defines the state of the share. For the purposes of creating a share, the lifecycleState will always be PUBLISHED.
Provides additional options while defining the content of the share.

Defines any visibility restrictions for the share. Possible values include: CONNECTIONS - The share will be viewable by 1st-degree connections only. PUBLIC - The share will be viewable by anyone on LinkedIn.
Values: CONNECTIONS - The share will be viewable by 1st-degree connections only.
PUBLIC - The share will be viewable by anyone on LinkedIn.

Rows.Text: Provides the primary content for the share.

Represents the media assets attached to the share. Possible values include: NONE - The share does not contain any media, and will only consist of text. ARTICLE - The share contains a URL. IMAGE - The Share contains an image.
Values: NONE - The share does not contain any media, and will only consist of text.
ARTICLE - The share contains a URL.
IMAGE - The Share contains an image.

Rows.Text: If the shareMediaCategory is ARTICLE or IMAGE, define those media assets here.
Provide a short description for your image or article.
ID of the uploaded image asset. If you are uploading an article, this field is not required.
Provide the URL of the article you would like to share here.
Customize the title of your image or article.

Blocks.Section: Create an Image or Video Share
SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Blocks.Text: If you'd like to attach an image or video to your share, you will first need to register, then upload your image/video to LinkedIn before the share can be created. We will walk through the following steps to create the share:

Blocks.Section: Create an Image or Video Share
SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Blocks.Text:
Register your image or video to be uploaded.
Upload your image or video to LinkedIn.
Create the image or video share.

SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Blocks.Text: Send a POST request to the assets API, with the action query parameter to registerUpload.

SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Blocks.Text: POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/assets?action=registerUpload

SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Blocks.Text: Similar to the author parameter we've used with the ugcPosts API, we will need to provide our Person URN. Additional recipes and serviceRelationships define the type of content we're publishing. For Share on LinkedIn, recipes will always contain either the type feedshare-image or the type feedshare-video (depending on which of the two you are uploading) and serviceRelationships will always define the relationshipType and identifier. See the request body below for reference.

SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Create an Image or Video Share
Blocks.Text: A successful response will contain an uploadUrl and asset that you will need to save for the next steps.

Blocks.Section: Upload Image or Video Binary File
SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Upload Image or Video Binary File
Blocks.Text: Using the uploadUrl returned from Step 1, upload your image or video to LinkedIn. To upload your image or video, send a POST request to the uploadUrl with your image or video included as a binary file. The example below uses cURL to upload an image file.

SectionPath: Create an Image or Video Share
Upload Image or Video Binary File
Blocks.Text: curl -i --upload-file /Users/peter/Desktop/superneatimage.png --header "Authorization: Bearer redacted" 'https://api.linkedin.com/mediaUpload/C5522AQGTYER3k3ByHQ/feedshare-uploadedImage/0?ca=vector_feedshare&cn=uploads&m=AQJbrN86Zm265gAAAWemyz2pxPSgONtBiZdchrgG872QltnfYjnMdb2j3A&app=1953784&sync=0&v=beta&ut=2H-IhpbfXrRow1'
